title: The Leeward Provision
premise: Edmund Yarrow, a mountain guide blacklisted after a rescue that ended in a government cover-up, is coerced into finding a vanished survey team in the remote Leeward Range. He discovers the team alive but hiding in a glacial cave, guarding evidence that the government itself caused an avalanche that buried a valley settlement — and that the 'survey' was a deliberate erasure of the proof. As officials close in to silence everyone, Edmund must choose between his own redemption and the survivors' safety, smuggling them out through terrain only he knows while the truth travels ahead of them by radio. The book ends with Edmund surrendering himself at the border so the evidence can cross without him, trading his freedom at last for the belonging he never believed he'd earned.
about_author: Jude Thackeray is the pen name of a former alpine rescue volunteer who writes adventure fiction from a farmhouse within sight of the ranges he once patrolled. His novels are known for austere prose, unforgiving landscapes, and protagonists who measure their worth in the people they bring home.

chapters.title: The Weight of Miles
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Fifteen years after his blacklisting, Edmund guides wealthy clients through the Leeward Range, counting his life in distance covered. A government liaison corners him at a trailhead lodge: a survey team has vanished, and his name is the only one cleared to enter the restricted zone. The beat: a man who trusts no one is offered a deal he cannot refuse.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with a brief interlude from surveyor Maren Oduya's field journal. Edmund reaches the team's last camp — tents intact, food untouched, boots gone, and no footprints leading out. A journal page hints the team found something and chose to disappear on purpose. The beat: dread curdling into the realization that the missing don't want to be found.

chapters.title: What the Glacier Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Following a hunch about meltwater channels, Edmund locates a cave system behind the glacier and finds four survivors: Maren, two technicians, and a dying geologist. They show him core samples and photographs proving the government detonated charges that triggered the avalanche burying Harrow Vale. The beat: the rescue becomes a moral ambush.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Flashback chapters within Maren's narration reveal how the team voted to hide rather than report, knowing the liaison's earlier expeditions ended in 'accidents.' Maren tests Edmund's motives, convinced a blacklisted guide can be bought. The beat: wary alliance forged in the dark, each holding a knife behind their back.

chapters.title: The Long White Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The five begin a night movement down a crevassed corridor while a government helicopter sweeps the ridge above. Edmund's knowledge of the ice is their only cover, but the dying geologist slows them past safety margins. The beat: Edmund discovers he cares about these people — and that caring is the most dangerous thing he's done in fifteen years.

chapters.title: Radio Silence, Broken
chapters.summary: POV Maren. A technician secretly transmits a fragment of the evidence to a journalist in the lowlands, forcing the team's hand: the government now knows someone is alive and talking. The liaison's voice comes through the radio offering Edmund full reinstatement if he delivers the team alone. The beat: temptation arrives wearing Edmund's own face — his old life, restored, for four strangers.

chapters.title: Harrow Vale
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The team detours through the buried valley, now a scar of rubble and provisional memorials, where Edmund meets a survivor of the avalanche who recognizes his name from the original cover-up. He learns his own blacklisting was engineered to discredit the one witness who might have spoken. The beat: grief and fury fuse into purpose; the inheritance of the dead becomes his to carry.

chapters.title: The Liaison's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Maren. The liaison and a small armed team intercept them at a river crossing, and Edmund bargains: himself in exchange for the others' safe passage. Maren realizes Edmund intends to be taken — and that the evidence must move without any of them. The beat: the plan crystallizes, cold and costly, and no one says goodbye properly.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The climax: a storm collapses the timetable, and Edmund leads the liaison's men into a whiteout while Maren's group splits the evidence across three routes to the border. Edmund turns the hunters' own reliance on him against them, walking them in circles until the storm and the mountain do the rest. The beat: the guide becomes the terrain itself.

chapters.title: The Leeward Provision
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, closing with Maren. At the border post, Edmund surrenders as the last evidence crosses in a mail sack; weeks later, the Harrow Vale findings break publicly and the inquiry begins. Maren testifies on his behalf, and his sentence is measured in months, not years. The beat: a man who measured life in miles finally measures it in years — and finds, for the first time, that he belongs to something.
